novelty_delta: Replace the abandoned learned-coordinate localization compiler with direct donor interchange of the exact full residual or module-output state at the final prediction position across two syntactic constructions. The screen asks whether one common site transfers both prepositional-phrase and relative-clause subject number while remaining small for noun-identity and attractor-number controls. The reusable scorer now derives C from the frozen task declaration: because Task 14 C preserves the answer, it measures absolute patched-versus-native movement normalized by the median A1/A2 donor effect, under the existing C ceiling. This preserves Task 14 semantics and adds a reusable causal localization step. Finding only that the state is distributed or robust would reproduce sections 1550-1552 and is not novel; novelty would require selective cross-syntax interchange at a specific boundary or a well-supported null under this stronger counterfactual.
decision_changed: The frozen authority is compatible with the reusable 55-site screen as a same-answer active C control. The answer-changing v2 C donors remain excluded from this adapter because they are complete-subject-number transfers expected to succeed, not unrelated controls. The seven native errors all occur in C, but both C direction cells have base and donor accuracies between 87.5% and 93.75%, above the current 75% per-cell threshold; every A1, A2, and P cell is 100%.
